answer: Topological Routing Cost Decay. Nodes establish multi-hop validation paths requiring distinct routing behavior across sparse subgraphs, akin to navigating a shifting dune. The enforcement rule scales latency penalties based on path convergence: when a cluster of agents routes transactions through overlapping neighbor sets, throughput drops exponentially for every redundant node. This design turns a sybil expansion into a costly voyage because duplicating connection endpoints forces the attacker to provision separate physical bandwidth and processing units for every branch of the vine.
